text_blocks.snippet: Recent active scams in Central Illinois include fake local contractor and garage door impersonators, fraudulent DMV text messages, and sheriff/arrest warrant phone threats.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake local contractor and garage door impersonators, fraudulent DMV text messages, and sheriff/arrest warrant phone threats

list.snippet:
Fake Garage Door Repair: Scammers use online search ads to pose as trusted local companies (like Bloomington's The Door Doctor), overcharging thousands for minor repairs or cutting hardware to fake extra damage
.

DMV/Secretary of State Texts: Fraudulent text messages claim recipients have unpaid driving fines or expiring licenses, telling victims to click a link and pay immediately. The state never texts for payment.
Law Enforcement & Warrant Calls: Callers pretend to be local sheriffs or legal agents claiming the target missed a court date or owes a bond, demanding payment via Bitcoin or cash apps.
Door-to-Door Storm Chasers: Transient contractors target neighborhoods after severe weather, demanding large cash deposits upfront or full advance payment without local licensing.
Verify phone numbers: Double-check contractor contact details independently rather than clicking the top sponsored web search result.

Practice the pause:
Take time to verify urgent demands for money or secrecy instead of reacting immediately.
Never pay by crypto or wire: Government agencies and legitimate utilities will never demand immediate payment via cryptocurrency, gift cards, or wire transfers.
